name: South Korea
seoTitle: History of South Korea: Miracle on the Han River, Taegeukgi Flag, and Democracy
metaDescription: Discover the detailed history of South Korea. Explore the Three Kingdoms, the 1948 Republic, the Taegeukgi Yin-Yang flag, and high-tech democracy.
mapFormation:
Occupying the southern half of the mountainous Korean Peninsula in East Asia across 100,363 square kilometers, the Republic of Korea (Daehan Minguk) is bounded by the Yellow Sea to the west, the Korea Strait to the south, and the Sea of Japan (East Sea) to the east.

Korean civilization traces its legendary foundation to Dangun Wanggeom in 2333 BCE (Gojoseon), followed by the Three Kingdoms period (Goguryeo, Baekje, and Silla) unified under Silla in 676 CE. In 1392, General Yi Seong-gye founded the Joseon Dynasty, which governed for over five centuries from its capital in Hanyang (modern Seoul) and oversaw the invention of the Korean Hangul alphabet by King Sejong the Great in 1443.

Following Japanese colonial rule (1910–1945) and the division of the peninsula along the 38th parallel at the end of World War II, the Republic of Korea was officially proclaimed on August 15, 1948. The modern de facto border with North Korea is the 250-kilometer-long Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), established by the 1953 Korean Armistice Agreement.
flagHistory:
The national flag of South Korea—the Taegeukgi—is a profound philosophical masterpiece of Taoist and Neo-Confucian cosmology, first used in 1882 by Joseon diplomats and officially adopted on October 15, 1949.

The flag features a pristine white field symbolizing peace, purity, and the traditional white clothing of the Korean people (the 'white-clad folk'). In the center sits the Taegeuk circle, divided horizontally into red (Yang - cosmic light, warmth, and masculine energy) at the top and blue (Yin - cosmic shadow, coolness, and feminine energy) at the bottom, representing universal harmony.

In the four corners are four black trigrams (Gwae) from the I Ching (Book of Changes): Geon (top-left: three solid lines = Heaven, Spring, Justice), Ri (bottom-left: Fire, Autumn, Wisdom), Gam (top-right: Water, Winter, Sincerity), and Gon (bottom-right: three broken lines = Earth, Summer, Vitality).
freedomStory:
South Korea's modern liberty represents an inspiring victory against foreign occupation and authoritarianism.

On March 1, 1919, millions of Koreans held peaceful mass demonstrations against Japanese colonial rule (the March 1st Movement), leading to the establishment of the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea in Shanghai.

Following the devastation of the Korean War (1950–1953), the nation achieved the phenomenal 'Miracle on the Han River', transforming from an impoverished agrarian war ruin into a high-tech industrial superpower. In June 1987, massive civic protests across Seoul forced the adoption of direct presidential elections and full constitutional democracy, creating a vibrant, high-tech society leading the world in semiconductors, shipbuilding, and global cultural arts (K-pop/K-dramas).
challenges: South Korea confronts profound demographic and geopolitical transformations. Foremost among them is the world's lowest total fertility rate, requiring innovative family welfare programs and eldercare automation. Technologically, Korea leads global AI memory chips while managing peninsula defense and clean nuclear and renewable transitions.

faqs.question: What is the meaning of the symbols on the South Korean flag (Taegeukgi)?
faqs.answer: The red and blue circle (Taegeuk) represents cosmic Yin-Yang harmony, while the four black trigrams in the corners represent Heaven, Earth, Water, and Fire.

faqs.question: What was the 'Miracle on the Han River'?
faqs.answer: The 'Miracle on the Han River' refers to the rapid post-war economic development and industrialization of South Korea between the 1960s and 1990s.

timeline.event: Legendary founding of Gojoseon by Dangun Wanggeom.
King Sejong the Great creates the scientific Hangul alphabet.
The March 1st Movement rallies nationwide for independence from Japanese colonial rule.
The Republic of Korea is officially established on August 15.
The Korean Armistice Agreement establishes the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ).
The June Democratic Struggle forces constitutional reforms for direct presidential elections.
Seoul hosts the Summer Olympic Games, demonstrating global economic emergence.
